title: Kapital Launcher manifest
description: What the launcher shows and launches: the chapter list, each chapter's pack and server, its wiki teaser and changelog. data/launcher.json is the copy built into the app; docs/adr/0004-launcher-manifest.md is the plan for the Kapitel Kapital site to publish the same shape. A manifest is untrusted input wherever it comes from: it can name things, never run them. There is no field for a command, a JVM argument or a path, and the Go loader refuses a URL that is not https on an allowlisted host, except a chapter's map, which may be http on a playit tunnel with a port (ADR-4, second amendment).

instanceId.description: A Prism instance id is its folder name. No separators, no dots-only names, nothing a path could be built from.

era.description: As the wiki's taxonomy writes the period.

jvm.description: A JVM preset the launcher owns, never raw arguments. zgc is -XX:+UseZGC -XX:+ZGenerational and needs Java 21, so Minecraft 1.20.5 or later.

packwiz.description: The hosted pack.toml packwiz-installer syncs from (ADR-3, option B).

mrpack.description: The .mrpack a fresh install imports (ADR-3, option A).

toggles.description: Mods a player may switch off from the chapter's settings as a quick choice (issue 156). Each names a mod and the start of its jar's file name; every jar in the instance's mods folder that starts with it is that mod, whichever version the pack ships. Names are unique, and no prefix starts another.

jarPrefix.description: The part of the jar's file name before its version, separator included: DistantHorizons- for DistantHorizons-3.3.3-1.21.1-fabric-neoforge.jar. A prefix, never a path or a pattern.

requires.description: The jarPrefix of another toggle of this chapter that this mod needs to load (Colorwheel needs Iris). With that one off, this one is off too and cannot be turned on. A chain of them must end.

addresses.description: Every address the server is reached at, the first being the default. The player picks one in the chapter's settings, saved as its label; the chosen address is pinged for the status line and, when the player turns on joining in the chapter's settings, passed to Prism's --server. Labels are unique within the chapter.

label.description: A short name the settings screen offers: Global, Germany. Never an address.

address.description: host[:port]. Passed to Prism's --server and dialled for the status line, so nothing else is accepted.

software.description: What the server runs, for the facts panel: Paper, Vanilla, or [PLACEHOLDER].

map.description: The chapter's BlueMap web map (issue 161). The one URL a manifest may give as http, and only on a playit tunnel (*.tun.ply.gg) with an explicit port; no user info, query or fragment. The launcher opens it in the system browser, frames it in a page and checks that it answers, nothing more. Optional: a chapter with no map leaves it out.
